backlog.spec: Supply jac for the objective (-1 on radii, 0 on centres) and an analytic constraint Jacobian (pair, wall and r>=0 rows) to minimize(). This removes finite-difference cost (about 78 evaluations per gradient), so many more restarts or iterations fit in 30 s.
backlog.title: Analytic Jacobian for SLSQP

backlog.spec: Keep cheap short SLSQP runs (maxiter 100) for screening. Then re-run SLSQP with maxiter 1000 and ftol 1e-12 from the top few results, and take the best after repair.
backlog.title: Raise MAX_ITER and polish best

backlog.spec: Initialise centres from a perturbed 5x5 grid plus one extra circle, or from staggered rows such as 5,5,6,5,5 with small gaussian noise (sd about 0.03). Use radii of about 0.09. Known good packings of 26 circles are near this structure.
backlog.title: Hex-like grid initialisation with jitter

backlog.spec: After an initial phase of restarts, repeatedly perturb the best solution (jitter centres by sd about 0.02, or relocate the smallest circle to a random place) and re-optimise with SLSQP. Accept the result if it improves.
backlog.title: Basin hopping from the best

backlog.spec: After SLSQP, fix the centres and solve an LP with scipy linprog for the maximum radii: maximise the sum of r subject to r_i+r_j<=d_ij, r_i<=wall distance, r>=0. Subtract 1e-12 for safety. This replaces the greedy shrink and recovers lost radius.
backlog.title: Smarter repair via exact LP radii

backlog.spec: Alternate between an LP for the radii at fixed centres and an SLSQP step on the centres. Use a trust-region move on the centres with a linearised constraint. This is a sequential LP scheme that often converges to tight packings.
backlog.title: Alternate LP radii and centre steps

backlog.spec: Write the pair constraint as d^2 - (ri+rj)^2 >= 0, together with ri+rj>=0 through r>=0. It is smooth at overlapping centres, so SLSQP is better conditioned. Add the analytic Jacobian.
backlog.title: Constraint on squared distances

backlog.spec: Draw initial radii at random from U(0.03,0.15) per circle instead of a constant 0.05. Mixing big and small circles explores the different radius distributions that good packings have.
backlog.title: Larger initial radii variety

backlog.spec: Raise TIME_FRACTION to 0.92. Break the loop when the predicted time for the next run exceeds the remaining time. The repair is cheap, so this gives more restarts safely under the 45 s cap.
backlog.title: Time fraction up to 0.93

backlog.spec: Start with a fast L-BFGS minimisation of a penalty energy: -sum r + mu*sum of squared overlaps, with mu increased 10x over 3 stages. Then run SLSQP from the result. It gives better starts than random points.
backlog.title: Two-stage penalty then SLSQP

backlog.spec: After a rough first SLSQP, keep only the pair constraints with d - ri - rj < 0.3 in a refinement run. The smaller constraint set speeds up each iteration. Verify the final result with the full repair.
backlog.title: Use only constraints for near pairs

backlog.spec: Generate starts with mirror symmetry about the diagonal or the vertical axis: sample 13 circles and reflect them, with some on the axis. Run SLSQP unconstrained from there. Optimal packings are often near-symmetric.
backlog.title: Symmetric initialisations

backlog.spec: For the best solution, delete the circle with the smallest radius. Find the largest hole by sampling 2000 random points and taking the max distance-based clearance. Put the circle there with small radius, and re-optimise.
backlog.title: Remove smallest and reinsert

backlog.spec: Run each restart with maxiter 60 first. If the sum of radii is below the best so far minus 0.03, discard it. Otherwise continue with maxiter 300 from that point.
backlog.title: Early termination of bad runs

backlog.spec: Reduce SHRINK to 1e-11 and make the repair loop iterate until no overlap above 1e-12 remains, with up to 500 iterations. Check the exact harness tolerance so that the packing stays valid. The gain is small but free.
backlog.title: Tighter safe shrink

backlog.spec: Compute the triu indices once at module level for each n and reuse them. Avoid temporary allocations in cons. This gives a minor speedup per call.
backlog.title: Vectorised pair-index caching

backlog.spec: Sample centres on the boundary band with probability 0.5 (one coordinate within 0.1 of an edge) and uniformly otherwise. Best packings put many circles on the walls and in the corners.
backlog.title: Border-biased initial centres

backlog.spec: Draw 26 random points. Apply 5 steps of Lloyd relaxation using a grid of 100x100 sample points to get an even spread. Use the result as centres with radius 0.5 times the nearest neighbour distance.
backlog.title: Lloyd relaxation start

backlog.spec: Use a callback that raises StopIteration when a single run exceeds 1.5 s of process time, then use the last iterate. Add a guard so that the last restart cannot overrun the limit.
backlog.title: Cap run length by wall time

backlog.spec: Keep the 5 best solutions of the random phase. In the second half of the time, perturb the pool members at random (sd 0.01 to 0.03) and re-optimise with SLSQP. This is an evolutionary refinement.
backlog.title: Seeded restarts keep top-k pool

backlog.spec: From the best solution, swap the positions of two circles of different radii (keep the radii, swap the centres), then re-optimise. Accept if it is better. This explores arrangements of big and small circles.
backlog.title: Swap-move of circles

backlog.spec: Polish the best SLSQP output with method trust-constr or SLSQP with ftol 1e-15, and tighter active constraints. Use it only if the polished result passes repair and is better.
backlog.title: Trust-constr final polish

backlog.spec: Add symmetry-breaking constraints r_i <= r_{i+1} (sorted radii) in SLSQP. This cuts the permutation symmetry and may help convergence. It is cheap to add.
backlog.title: Vary penalty on radii ordering

backlog.spec: Start with 20 circles with radius 0.1 on a jittered grid and 6 tiny circles (radius 0.01) at random. SLSQP then grows the small ones into the interstices.
backlog.title: Small-circle seeding in gaps

backlog.spec: Set options ftol=1e-10 in SLSQP so that the runs stop earlier when converged, or loosen to 1e-7 for the screening runs. This saves time per restart.
backlog.title: Multiple ftol settings

backlog.spec: Take the best solution. Scale the centres about (0.5,0.5) by 0.9 and radii by 0.9, add noise sd 0.005, and re-optimise. This shakes jams loose.
backlog.title: Compress and expand cycle

backlog.spec: Draw random centres, solve an LP for the optimal radii at those centres, then start SLSQP from centres and LP radii. The start is feasible, which helps SLSQP behave.
backlog.title: Radii-only LP warm start

backlog.spec: Before SLSQP, shrink the initial radii until all constraints hold (r_i = 0.5*min distance to neighbours or the wall). A feasible start avoids early large steps.
backlog.title: Feasible start via shrink

backlog.spec: If the best has not improved by more than 1e-6 in the last 30 restarts, switch the remaining time to basin hopping around the best, using perturbation sd 0.01.
backlog.title: Parallel-free early stop on plateau

incumbent.description: After 40% of the time on random restarts, perturb the best packing (centre jitter sd 0.02 or relocating the smallest circle) and re-run SLSQP, keeping improvements.
